hook: Mopping with drinking water is *No. 1* on the water board's complaint app
hook_b: Mopping with drinking water is *No. 1* on the water board's complaint app
tldr: Four weeks after HMWSSB launched its PAANI app, mopping with drinking water or groundwater is the most reported misuse, mostly from Jubilee Hills and Banjara Hills.

beats.what: About 75 of 250-plus complaints filed on HMWSSB's PAANI app in four weeks are about people mopping homes with drinking water or groundwater.
beats.why: The app, launched on October 29, lets residents photograph and report water misuse; field teams now verify every complaint in person.
beats.care: Violators are fined Rs 1,000 to Rs 20,000; notices come first, and unpaid fines are added to the water bill.

causes.label: Drinking water used to mop and wash

effects.label: Unpaid fines go on water bill

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Officials found some residents using pressure motors on drinking water lines to wash floors and driveways, mostly in the mornings.

cards.q: Rs 1,000-20,000 fines for wasting drinking water: fair call?

qs: How many of the 250-plus complaints ended in a fine?
Does groundwater mopping count the same as drinking-water mopping?

facts.t: The app covers *10* kinds of violations, from illegal motors to overflowing tanks.

viz.verdict: Mopping leads the complaints; leakages are a close second.

viz.l: How a complaint turns into a fine
viz.verdict: Residents who waste drinking water face fines; others report it.

watch: Field teams show violators the complainant's photos and videos, serve a notice, then add any unpaid fine to the water bill.
